channel.title: Farsçadan (English)
channel.description: AI-assisted English translations of selected stories from Iran's Persian-language press. Every story notes the outlet's political orientation.

item.title: Weekly Framework (November 16-22): Blockade breached at Hormuz, regional fire reignited in the Gulf
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Persian press this week: oil flow halved at Hormuz, renewed fire exchanges in Bahrain-Riyadh-Jeddah, Abadan protests and winter hardship. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: Iran's nuclear program: what are the NPT, the JCPOA, and the 'trigger mechanism'?
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: NPT, IAEA oversight, JCPOA limits, enrichment rates, and the snapback mechanism explained chronologically from 1970 to 2026. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: IRGC claims Patriot radar strike on Bahrain bases; Bahrain and U.S. do not confirm
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Iran's IRGC announced striking two Patriot radars at U.S. bases in Bahrain; Bahrain called UN Security Council meeting. (Source: Khabaronline)

item.title: Fidan: Iran-U.S. deal more important than opening Hormuz
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Foreign Minister Fidan said an Iran-U.S. agreement matters beyond reopening Hormuz; war's financial burden strains nations. (Source: Khabaronline)

item.title: Qatar mediation continues: delegation in Tehran, Pakistan and Germany-Qatar joint statement
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: A Qatari delegation visited Tehran; Pakistan's FM hopeful on deal; Qatar-Germany issued joint statement on Iran. (Source: Ettelaat)

item.title: Abu Dhabi's ADNOC bypasses Hormuz blockade with U.S. support, oil flow halved
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: WSJ: ADNOC carries oil from Hormuz with U.S. military support; FT reports flow dropped 50% in second week of November. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Homemade alcohol poisoning in Nishapur: 33 hospitalized, 3 deaths
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: 33 people poisoned in Nishapur from homemade alcohol; 3 deaths reported, two with brain death confirmed. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: What is the Revolutionary Guard (Sepah): structure, Basij and Quds Force, difference from Artesh
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Structure, branches, Basij and Quds Force relationship, and differences from the regular army, with sourced figures. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: Araghchi: Strait of Hormuz reopening requires 7 conditions, 'neither war nor peace' must end
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Foreign Minister Araghchi says 7 conditions apply to Strait of Hormuz reopening; states 60% enriched uranium will not leave Iran. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: CENTCOM warns Trump: Window for Iran attack is rapidly closing
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Per Financial Times, CENTCOM told Trump administration that time window and resources for Iran military action are narrowing; Israel pressing for new ops. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Fairford trial: New York defendant shouts 'We are Qasem Soleimani's army' in court
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: In RAF Fairford plot trial, New York defendant disrupts court shouting nationalist slogans; London defendants' lawyers say will likely contest charges. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: U.S. Treasury's dual move: Singapore-Malaysia warning and sanctions on 4 Iranians
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: U.S. Treasury warns Singapore and Malaysia about Iran-linked shell companies; sanctions 4 Iranians including football federation head's brother. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Two-hour power blackout in Tehran: Officials blame 'grid maintenance'
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Tehran Electric Distribution announced 2-hour blackout for November 21; officials attribute it to grid maintenance as winter energy crisis deepens. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Who decides in Iran? A map of six institutions and their powers
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Guide to the powers of the Supreme Leader, President, Parliament, Guardian Council, Expediency Council, and Assembly of Experts, with sources. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: U.S. Senate rejects resolution to limit Trump's Iran war powers again
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Senate votes 48-51 to reject resolution restricting Trump's Iran military ops; Pennsylvania Democrat Fetterman broke ranks. This is the 12th vote this year. (Source: ISNA)

item.title: Riyadh's tallest tower hit in Houthi attack; Saudis confirm damage
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Saudi civil defense confirmed a tower in Riyadh's financial center was struck in a Houthi attack; no casualties reported. (Source: Donya-ye Eqtesad)

item.title: Iran strikes back at Vienna: won't return to pre-war inspection terms
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Iran's IAEA representative criticized the agency's silence on U.S.-Israeli strikes; U.S. and three European nations demanded inspectors return. (Source: Ettelaat)

item.title: Iran tries oil exports through blockade? TankerTrackers claim lacks confirmation
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: TankerTrackers claimed Iran is preparing to resume crude oil exports despite naval blockade; no official confirmation received. (Source: Donya-ye Eqtesad)

item.title: Pezeshkian says "I sleep in a coat," gets sharp backlash from struggling citizens
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Iran's President Pezeshkian said he sleeps in a coat without heat as an example of energy conservation; struggling citizens attacked the remark on social media. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Iran's press map: which newspaper, which faction's voice?
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: From IRNA to Kayhan, from Hamshahri to Iran International: a map of Iranian media's ownership and political orientation. (Source: Farsçadan)
